observations.text: SP performed the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only, with the IP directing the pitch and power corrections throughout both turns. Altitude departed by 350 feet and bank by 12 degrees before the IP's direction restored the parameters, which remains within the expected standard for this Training Section. Marginal performance; the altitude trend was recognized late on each turn, and self-recognition of the trend before the IP's direction is expected on the next sortie.

SP entered and completed both steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only without the IP directing or executing any part of the maneuver. Altitude was contained at 300 feet and airspeed at 20 knots from the entry values, at the published tolerance limits, with the deviations recognized and corrected after the IP's verbal prompts alone. Control of the aircraft remained with SP throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP established and flew the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only, maintaining the instrument cross-check without verbal prompting. Deviations were limited to 200 feet of altitude, 15 knots of airspeed and 8 degrees of bank, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Rollout after the 360 degree heading change was completed 8 degrees past the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew both steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only with an accurate and rapid instrument cross-check between attitude, altimeter and airspeed. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and bank within 4 degrees, with rollout within 4 degrees of the entry heading after the 360 degree heading change. No IP prompt was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only with exceptional precision, setting pitch and power ahead of each bank change. Altitude, airspeed, bank and rollout heading were maintained with negligible deviations, not exceeding 40 feet, 3 knots, 2 degrees of bank and 2 degrees on rollout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an entry technique that established the bank before the power increase required for the 60 degree turn, did not maintain the entry altitude and airspeed during the steep turn. Altitude decayed by 400 feet and airspeed by 25 knots, both beyond the published tolerances, with the result that the IP set the power and directed the recovery to level flight. Repetition of the entry sequence, with power applied before bank passes 45 degrees, is required.

SP, due to situational awareness limited to the instrument in use, without reference to the wider aircraft state, held attention on the attitude indicator and did not cross-check the altimeter and airspeed inside the 60 degree bank turn. The turn developed into a descending spiral with altitude loss beyond 500 feet, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to arrest the descent and reestablish level flight. The maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP performed the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only and completed both turns within the standards for this Training Section, following the IP's verbal prompts on altitude and bank. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and bank 10 degrees, at the tolerance limits, and each deviation was recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance; earlier detection of the altitude trend from the vertical speed indication, and correction without the IP's prompt, is expected on the following sortie.

SP entered and flew the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only without any verbal prompt from the IP. Deviations were limited to 220 feet of altitude, 14 knots of airspeed and 7 degrees of bank, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Rollout after the 360 degree heading change was completed within 8 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew both steep turns on instrument references only with an accurate and rapid cross-check, holding the briefed 45 degree and 60 degree bank angles without prompting. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and bank within 4 degrees, with rollout within 4 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy on both steep turns on instrument references only, with pitch and power set before the bank was established and the cross-check sustained throughout the 360 degree heading change. Deviations were negligible, not exceeding 40 feet of altitude, 3 knots of airspeed, 2 degrees of bank and 2 degrees on the rollout heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an inadequate pitch and power correction on entry to the 60 degree bank turn, did not maintain the entry altitude and airspeed required for steep turns on instrument references only. Altitude loss exceeded 400 feet and airspeed increased by 30 knots, both beyond the published limits, with the result that the IP set the power and directed the recovery. The maneuver was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with aircraft control, radio work and the heading count attempted simultaneously, did not sustain the instrument cross-check through the 360 degree heading change of the steep turn. Bank increased 12 degrees past the briefed 60 degrees and altitude departed by more than 350 feet, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to reestablish the parameters and executed the rollout. Task shedding under increasing workload is to be briefed and practised before the next repetition.

SP, due to a trim technique that left the aircraft out of trim at the entry to each turn, did not hold the briefed bank and the entry altitude without prompting. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and bank 10 degrees, at the published tolerance limits, and the parameters were restored only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction of the deviations occurred with delay.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the attitude indicator, did not monitor altitude and airspeed inside the 60 degree bank turn. Airspeed departed by 20 knots and altitude by 300 feet, at the published limits, with the result that both were corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, without IP intervention on the controls.

SP performed the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only within the standards for this Training Section, without IP's intervention. Altitude deviation twice reached 250 feet and bank 8 degrees, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner, and rollout after the 360 degree heading change was completed 8 degrees past the entry heading. Marginal performance; a faster cross-check rate on the altimeter and an established lead point for rollout are expected to bring the deviations inside 150 feet and 5 degrees on the next sortie.

SP flew both steep turns on instrument references only with an accurate and rapid cross-check and correct pitch, power and bank control throughout. Altitude was held within 130 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and bank within 4 degrees, with rollout within 5 degrees of the entry heading after the 360 degree heading change. No IP prompt or intervention was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the steep turns at 45 degrees and 60 degrees of bank on instrument references only with exceptional precision, anticipating the pitch and power requirement at each change of bank. Altitude, airspeed, bank and rollout heading were maintained with negligible deviations, not exceeding 40 feet, 3 knots and 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.
